record.paper_title: The origin and evolution of transition discs: successes, problems and open questions
record.original_question: If giant planets create mm-bright transition discs, what physical mechanism removes or traps enough 1–10 micron dust from the inner disc to suppress the near-infrared excess while still leaving a mm cavity, maintaining active accretion onto the star, and remaining consistent with scattered-light and thermal-infrared observations?

evidence.quote: Thus, dust filtration alone cannot remove small 1 − 10 µm dust particles.

This is problematic as small particles dominate the opacity, so if they indeed follow the gas through the gap and populate the inner disc then the disc will show a strong IR-excess at all wavelengths and have an SED consistent with a primordial disc.
One must find a model that produces a mm ring, scattered light image consistent with the SEEDs structure, a lack of NIR excess and active accretion.

artifact.status_search_result: The literature confirms this remains an open modelling problem: dust filtration by a planet-induced pressure bump can trap mm grains but does not remove well-coupled 1–10 micron grains, and reviews continue to list the simultaneous reproduction of an mm ring, depleted NIR excess, ongoing accretion, and observed scattered-light structure as an unresolved challenge. Candidate ingredients (radiation pressure, dust growth in the inner disc, multiple planets, MHD winds, photoevaporation) have been proposed but no single self-consistent model has been demonstrated to satisfy all constraints simultaneously.

status_evidence.title: Transition disks: the observational revolution from SEDs to imaging
status_evidence.snippet: Dissimilarities in the spatial distribution of small (μm-size) and large (mm-size) dust grains have recently been pointed out; some transition disks present a strong near-infrared excess.
status_evidence.claim: Recent reviews still treat the differential spatial distribution of small versus large grains in transition discs and the origin of the NIR-excess dichotomy as an active open question.

status_evidence.title: Small vs. large dust grains in transitional disks: do different cavity sizes indicate a planet? (SAO 206462)
status_evidence.snippet: Different cavity sizes for small and large grains in transitional discs.
status_evidence.claim: Observations show distinct cavity sizes for micron- and mm-sized dust, motivating but not resolving the mechanism question.

status_evidence.title: Ring shaped dust accumulation in transition disks
status_evidence.snippet: A pressure bump at the outer edge of a planetary gap can trap millimetre-sized particles, but small grains follow the gas through the gap.
status_evidence.claim: Filtration retains mm grains but not 1–10 micron grains, leaving the suppression of NIR excess unexplained by filtration alone.
